newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - SOUTH AFRICA - AUGUST 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - SOUTH AFRICA - AUGUST 7.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Thursday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
BUSINESS DAY
- The South African Revenue service is about to get a new weapon in its struggle against tax evasion -- a computer system which could make taxes and death equally certain.

- Legislation making it virtually impossible for repeat serious offenders to obtain bail and to force experienced court officials to hear bail applications in murder, rape and robbery cases, was approved by the cabinet on Wednesday.

- New Africa Investments (Nail) gained 95 percent ownership of The Sowetan on Wednesday through the acquisition of publishing group Independent Newspapers ' remaining 42,5 percent stake in the newspaper for 63,1 million rand.

- Thousands of teachers took to the streets on Wednesday, causing disruptions to schools countrywide, while government was assessing whether additional funds were available for further increases for all public service workers.
- Agriculture and Land Affairs Minister Derek Hanekom suspended the 13 members of the Meat Board on Wednesday, citing dissatisfaction with the management of the deregulation of the meat industry.
BUSINESS REPORT

- Sentrachem's board and large shareholder Old Mutual are reserving judgment on Dow Chemical's two billion rand offer to take over Sentrachem, as market sentiment grows that shareholders could do better than the offered 10,50 rand a share.
- Anglo American Industrial Corporation (Amic), which experienced its best quarter ever at the end of last year, turned in an 8 percent increase on Wednesday in first-half headline earnings.

- The Competition Baord would on Thursday meet the liquidators of New New Age Beverages, the failed Pepsi bottler, to discuss the implicationsof selling the plant to one of the market leaders, Pierre Brooks, the chairman of the board, said.

- Retail sales remained firm in May when nominal sales surged 14,5 percent and real sales gained 5,5 percent from the same month a year ago, according to figures released on Wednesday by the Central Statistical Service (CSS).
- Tsogo Sun, the gambling group, has proposed converting the old Johannesburg Sun hotel, now trading as a Holiday Inn Garden Court, into a hotel and gambling school.
SAKE BEELD
- Steps should be taken soon by the South African Reserve Bank to ensure that the economy grows moderately instead of experiencing a complete recession.

- Amic has increased its interim net earnings for the six months to end June by 24 percent to 507 million rand. Its net earnings per share have, however, risen by only eight percent to 658 cents due to the increase of issued shares.

- Hundreds of doctors, chemists and members of the South African Police Service will be prosecuted soon under allegations of huge fraud which has been uncovered lately at Polmed, the police medical aid fund.

- The South African Department of Agriculture will exercise much stricter control over loans granted to farmers. This follows the huge losses that the department experienced over the past years due to farmers who do not settle their debts.
- The rand, which weakened by nearly 3 cents against the American dollar, strengthened again in the afternoon after the dollar lost against the Deutsch Mark.
THE STAR
- Chaos broke out in KwaThema, Springs, on Wednesday when angry youths, venting their frustration over electricity cuts stoned cars and set a Telkom van alight.
- Former state president P W Botha (81) is in love, and the rumour is that he is planning to marry a widow 31 years his junior from Graaff-Reinet in the Eastern Cape.

- Intelligence sources on Wednesday linked the gang responsible for a string of military-style highway heists to a covert former Umkhonto weSizwe cell that operated in North West Province during the apartheid era.

- Ground-breaking draft legislation severely restricting access to bail by suspects accused of serious crimes such as murder, rape involving children, and car hijacking was approved by the cabinet on Wednesday.
